walkthroughs.body_html:
River Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

River Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with River Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why do meanders migrate across a floodplain?
options: Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Meanders form because rivers flow around obstacles like rocks.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Faster water on the outside of the bend causes erosion (river cliff); slower water on the inside causes deposition (slip-off slope) — over time the channel shifts laterally.

mcqs.q: What is lag time on a storm hydrograph?
options: Lag time is how long the storm itself lasts.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.

mcqs.q: What is hydraulic action in a river?
options: The force of moving water itself compressing air into cracks in the river bank or bed, weakening rock until pieces break off — no sediment needed.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Hydraulic action is when rocks in the river smash into each other.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polar Environments”?
options: High latitude regions with permanent ice; Arctic (sea ice over ocean) vs Antarctic (ice on continent); minus 60 degrees C possible.
Subarctic biome with permafrost subsoil; short summers allow lichens, mosses, grasses; reindeer, musk ox, lemmings.
Permanently frozen ground covering 25% of Northern Hemisphere; thawing releases methane, threatens infrastructure.
Plants adapted to drought: deep tap roots (mesquite), water storage (cacti), waxy leaves; reduce transpiration.
